title: Rappolo, Bee Palmer's act and the first band at Friars Inn
summary: Brunis recalls Rappolo's girlfriend, Bee Palmer's shimmy act, and who made up the first band at Friars Inn.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, can you tell me a little bit about Rap? Had he been, uh, living in Davenport, working on a boat, or what?
Well, he was working in Davenport somewhere, and he was going with this young, beautiful, blonde girl, and, uh, she, I think she was killed in an automobile accident.
Well, do you remember something about, uh, B. Palmer, too? Oh, well, that's the... She had brought him up or something, do you remember?

Yeah, that's right. B. Palmer, and it was Santo Picora, who is now at the, uh, famous door. Emmett Hardy on trumpet, there was the trumpet boy. Uh, Leona Paula, Frisco on drums, no, Martin Burke on drums, and, uh, Al Siegel on piano. And she had a shimmy act that went out in vaudeville, and it was a wonderful act. And, uh, then Rap, uh, that, that thing broke up. It lasted a pretty good long time, a couple of years on the off-room circuit. And then Rap left, and that's when we, when we got him in, uh, Davenport. And then we left the boat, and then we went, we got the offer to go into Fryers Inn. And the, uh, the first band to go into Fryers Inn was, uh, Paul Merez, Leon Rapola, Elmer Schoble on piano, uh, Frank Snyder on drums, uh, Louis Black on banjo, who was now a police officer in Davenport, I think. And, uh, Steve Brown. No, it was Arnold Lake Canna first. And then that band split up, and Elmer went out to the Midway, oh, we were there for three years, I think. No, two years. Elmer went out to the Midway Gardens with his own band, and Snyder left and went somewhere, I don't know where he went, and, uh, let's see. We, we got, uh, Mel Stitzel on piano. Yeah, with Captain Daniel.
